third_party/sentencepiece — PROVENANCE
=======================================

upstream_url:       https://github.com/google/sentencepiece

scope
-----
Full vendored tree at tag v0.2.0, minus:
  - .git/      (no in-tree git history)
  - .github/   (CI workflow YAML not needed for our build)
  - data/      (~37 MB of corpus samples used only by upstream CLI tests;
                excluded to keep our tree small; not needed for libsentencepiece)
  - python/    (Python bindings; from the measured path; not built)
  - doc/       (Markdown documentation not consumed by our build)

NOT linked into bpe_runner:
  - spm_train       CLI binary
  - spm_encode      CLI binary
  - spm_decode      CLI binary
  - TensorFlow op   (SPM_ENABLE_TENSORFLOW_SHARED=OFF)
  - Python bindings (excluded at vendoring time)
  - Unigram trainer subcommands (architecturally still compiled into
    libsentencepiece since they share the trainer-spec scaffolding; not
    invoked by our runner — runner call-site + CI grep audit on runners/bpe/)

bundled snapshots (in-tree; no git submodules)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Single PROVENANCE-per-upstream rule preserved — these are upstream-bundled
slices that ship inside the SentencePiece source tarball at tag v0.2.0:

  third_party/absl/
    license:   Apache-2.0
    contents:  absl::container, absl::flags, absl::strings slices used by
               SentencePiece's CLI flag parsing + memory utilities.

  third_party/protobuf-lite/
    license:   BSD-3-Clause-Google (Google 2008 BSD-style; "Copyright 2008
               Google Inc. All rights reserved. Redistribution and use ...
               permitted provided that the following conditions are met:
               * Redistributions of source code must retain the above
               copyright ..."). NOT Apache-2.0: protobuf-lite is BSD-3-Clause. Permissive.
    contents:  Minimal protobuf-lite runtime used by SentencePiece's
               ModelProto serialization. SPM_PROTOBUF_PROVIDER="internal"
               (v0.2.0 option name) selects this bundled copy.

  third_party/darts_clone/
    license:   BSD (2008-2011 Susumu Yata; standard BSD)
    contents:  darts.h — Double-ARray Trie System header-only library used
               by SentencePiece for vocabulary trie lookup. Plan §17 scope-
               fence forbids PieceToId/IdToPiece invocation from runners/bpe/
               (the only call-paths that materially exercise darts_clone in
               the measured region).

  third_party/esaxx/
    license:   MIT-style (2010 Daisuke Okanohara; permissive)
    contents:  esa.hxx + sais.hxx — Enhanced Suffix Array library used by
               SentencePiece's BPE trainer for substring counting during
               pair-merge iteration. THIS IS DIRECTLY ON THE PATH — esaxx's SA construction is the dominant cost of
               SentencePieceTrainer::Train at large V × large N (and the
               source of the . Confirmed to be a
               headline dependency (not optional).

phase_4_bpe_adjusted_decision_1
-------------------------------
The 1.x
CMake option name `SPM_USE_BUILTIN_PROTOBUF=ON`. SentencePiece v0.2.0
renamed this option to `SPM_PROTOBUF_PROVIDER="internal"` and added a new
sibling option `SPM_ABSL_PROVIDER="internal"`. Behaviour identical (selects
the bundled snapshots over a system installation). Our CMake shim uses the
new option names. Recorded here per the Phase 4 "adjusted decision, not
re-litigation" convention.

protobuf_lite_license_note
--------------------------
The file at third_party/protobuf-lite/LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause-Google
("Copyright 2008 Google Inc. ... Redistribution and use in source and
binary forms, with or without modification, are permitted ..."). Still
permissive; net bpe_runner binary license unchanged (Apache-2.0 dominant
in the static-link graph).

No Apple clang / libc++ portability patches were required. SentencePiece
v0.2.0 builds clean on macOS Darwin 24 / Apple clang 17 / libc++ / C++17.

byte_fallback_roundtrip_note (load-bearing for the BPE baseline design)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
SentencePiece v0.2.0 with `byte_fallback=true` + `normalization=identity`
does NOT round-trip lone high-bit non-UTF-8 bytes: an empirical probe
against this vendored snapshot shows bytes 0xFF and 0x80 decoding as
U+FFFD (UTF-8 `EF BF BD`):

    Train: 200 sentences of 32 bytes each (high-bit content),
           --vocab_size=512 --byte_fallback=true --normalization_rule_name=identity
           --add_dummy_prefix=false --remove_extra_whitespaces=false
           --character_coverage=1.0 --hard_vocab_limit=false
           --unk_id=0 --bos_id=-1 --eos_id=-1 --pad_id=-1
           --input_format=text --split_by_whitespace=false
           --treat_whitespace_as_suffix=false
           --allow_whitespace_only_pieces=true

    Encode input bytes:  00 61 0a FF 62 80                       (N=6)
    Encoded IDs:         1 401 486 385 465 385                   (FF and 80 both -> ID 385)
    Decode output bytes: 00 61 0a EF BF BD 62 EF BF BD           (FF, 80 -> U+FFFD)

For this reason the harness's `bpe` baseline does not feed raw bytes to
SentencePiece. It drives SentencePiece BPE through the GPT-2 byte<->unicode
bijection (bytes_to_unicode + a 256-codepoint coverage line +
character_coverage=1.0), which round-trips arbitrary bytes (verified over
0x00..0xFF including lone 0x80/0xFF/NUL/newline by the exhaustive fuzzer in
tests/bpe_roundtrip_test.cpp). minbpe (third_party/minbpe) serves as a
secondary test-only round-trip cross-check. Configuration rationale:
docs/benchmark/fairness/bpe.md.

reproducibility_caveat
----------------------
Double-anchored: tag `v0.2.0` plus the explicit HEAD SHA recorded above.
No transitive submodules to track (all third_party/ contents are flat
snapshots inside the SentencePiece tarball, not git submodules).
